r1_closure.evidence: G1.4 now chooses c₀ and x₀, constructs a horizontal section over C̃, evaluates there, and proves scalar deck invariance exactly characterizes descent to C. A separately supplied section on C is a distinct allowed input. EN/JA APIs require the same proof; a sign-monodromy diagnostic was added.

M1.2 explicitly adds Hausdorffness and second countability, retains separation information in the broader analytic category, and requires verification for N/M objects. A fixed-model-dimension qualification is still needed; see GR2-01.

M2.3 uses affine square-zero thickenings, identifies the ideal by flatness, retains H² obstruction/H¹ torsor/H⁰ automorphisms, proves relative higher-direct-image vanishing, and invokes the affine base and Leray. General bases use open/fppf descent. No absolute nonaffine H² vanishing is asserted.

M1.2 compares positive powers and bases by a common multiple. M2.1 separately compares both constructed Quot/GIT presentations through their proved universal properties, with composition and base-change laws. No M1.2→M2.1 proof dependency remains.

N1.5 consumes TauCeti.exists_frobenius_flat_coordinate and owns the h→graph, curvature→integrability and gluing adapter. M1.2 now names coherent cohomology, proper direct images and only the SSF4.12 chow_lemma branch; the unrelated flattening/StableReduction branch is excluded explicitly.

G1.4 now excludes Part P, not the merged roadmap owner. Its general transport references explicitly say N1.5/N1.6; the appendix uses N1.5 for groupoid/descent. The declared graph has the intended separation.
N1.6 restricts zero-form degeneracy to positive-dimensional fibers and explicitly states nondegeneracy on a zero-dimensional vertical tangent space in both languages.

The optional observer label and the identified completion/availability-status prose are removed. M2.3/M3.4 state mathematical dependency/construction requirements; G1.4 is an in-scope conditional theorem and JA Law3 says 証明する. The P-target hypotheses moved from the JA appendix into the corresponding local targets are preserved.
JA now uses 2-圏的な整合性を伴う降下 and 2同型の整合性 in the relevant M1.1/M3.3/constructive-requirement passages; it no longer describes bicategorical coherence as two construction stages.
Both language source lists and sources.toml include the April1971 Deligne erratum and its exact deleted/replacement scope, while retaining the valid one-dimensional and II6.6 claims.

remaining_findings.title: Native manifold comparison still needs fixed complex dimension or componentwise construction
locations: README.ja.md M1.2 corresponding first supporting construction
remaining_findings.evidence: The amended comparison applies to smooth Hausdorff second-countable analytic spaces, but the native CKG IsManifold carrier has a fixed finite-dimensional model. Smooth analytic spaces can have connected components of different dimensions.
remaining_findings.counterexample: The disjoint union ℂ ⊔ ℂ² is smooth, Hausdorff and second countable, but is not a manifold with one fixed model ℂ^n.
remaining_findings.required_change: State the comparison for smooth analytic spaces of a fixed complex dimension n, or decompose by the locally constant dimension and construct the native manifold on each open-and-closed dimension part. Verify fixed dimension for each admitted native N/M application. This preserves all mathematical scope used here.
remaining_findings.source_scope: ComplexKahlerGeometry K3 explicitly partitions smooth strata by constant complex dimension and connected components before giving a single fixed-dimensional manifold model (current README around lines422–429).
remaining_findings.relation_to_r1: Completes the native-carrier hypothesis precision requested in GR1-02; the Hausdorff and second-countability repairs themselves are correct.

regression_review: No further defect found in the revised universal-cover observation theorem, affine Picard argument, polarization proof order, local target hypotheses, N1.5 native reuse, Deligne correction, P1–P6 retained scope or the A1.7 crosscheck. The final fixed-model qualification is the only remaining geometry review finding.
